Shell execution is blocked in this session, so I couldn't run the build myself — but the implementation is complete and I verified the logic manually against every test case.

## What I implemented

**`kindergarten_garden.h`** — declares the `Plants` enum (`clover`, `grass`, `violets`, `radishes`) and the function the tests call:

```cpp
std::array<Plants, 4> plants(const std::string& garden, const std::string& student);
```

**`kindergarten_garden.cpp`** — the implementation:
- Splits the garden string into two rows at the `\n`.
- Looks up the student's index in the fixed alphabetical roster (Alice … Larry, 12 students).
- Each student owns cups at positions `index * 2` and `index * 2 + 1` in each row.
- Returns `{row1[cup], row1[cup+1], row2[cup], row2[cup+1]}` mapped from `G`/`C`/`R`/`V` via a small `to_plant` switch.

I traced all 16 test cases by hand (including the full 24-cup garden for every student from Alice through Larry) and the expected arrays match.

To build and run the tests, run:

```bash
cmake -S . -B build -DEXERCISM_RUN_ALL_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build
./build/kindergarten-garden
```

If you can approve shell access, I'm happy to run that and confirm all tests pass.
